content:
If you've recently purchased a new Mac, like the recently released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you're likely on the hunt for a new external display.

Below are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories, different price points, and more options.

The best external Mac displays

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to a roundup of the best displays on the market, the Apple Studio Display is a must-mention. Although it carries a premium price tag, it features Apple's signature sleek design and comes with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts display color temperature based on ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display is available in multiple configurations at different price points, which I've listed below. If you want an iMac-like experience to pair with your Mac, nothing beats the Apple Studio Display.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR launched earlier this year and offers several key advantages over the standard Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness, 2,000 nits HDR peak brightness
  • Color support: P3 and Adobe RGB wide color gamut, supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz with Adaptive Sync
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

These advantages naturally make it more expensive than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor, with its 4K OLED panel, is a very attractive option for Mac users. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn has already made the switch, saying that "it's been a pleasure to use with my Mac mini over the past few months."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although it doesn't offer the 5K or 6K sharpness of some options on this list, you can enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks and better color reproduction and contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K is an evolution of LG's high-end development in the display business. It offers a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels, and a generous port selection. Here are the main specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone technology: None; supports auto-brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

Below are the purchase links for the LG UltraFine 6K

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin tried this one in person, and it immediately caught my attention. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K display offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) and similar 27-inch size, but at half the price of the Studio Display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensors auto-adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C supporting DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

You can check out Jeff's full review above for all the details. If you're looking for a 5K display to pair with your Mac, the Asus ProArt is truly hard to beat.

Below are the purchase links for the Asus ProArt Display 5K:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you want a larger, higher-resolution option, Asus has you covered too. The new Asus ProArt Display 6K (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly good value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

Perhaps the most appealing aspect of the ASUS ProArt 6K display is its price. It's noticeably cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K displays on the market.

Below are the purchase links for the ASUS ProArt 6K display:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

The Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Adaptive Picture auto-adjusts brightness based on ambient lighting
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Below are the purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Display

This might be my current favorite on this list. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K display comes packed with Mac-friendly features, headlined by its crisp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: Typical and peak 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller supporting custom controls

Below are the purchase links for the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K display:

Read our full review: BenQ's 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 Designer Display is a true Apple Studio Display competitor

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Display

If you're looking for a 32-inch display to pair with your new Mac on a budget under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. However, its biggest drawback is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. That said, it comes with a rich port selection, and the 32-inch panel is priced under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Below are the purchase links for the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt display:

Read our full review: Should the 32-inch 4K Mac display really be left out?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch UltraWide

If you want to pair your Mac with an ultra-wide display, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display. It also comes with a generous port selection, a matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz with VRR support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light sensor auto-adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Below are the purchase links for the Dell U4025QW 40-inch UltraWide:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

If you want to enter the ultra-wide market at a more affordable price, the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is an option, and it's currently on sale at nearly half price. It doesn't offer as many features as other options, but you can still enjoy a 34-inch ultra-wide curved display, along with a generous port selection including a Thunderbolt 4 port that supports power delivery.

  • Display: 34-inch ultra-wide curved display with Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature, delivering an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits.
  • Camera: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Below are the purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC:

Conclusion

The above is just a selection of the best external display options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, plenty of connectivity options, and unique sizes and designs.

Have you recently bought a new Mac? Which display are you using to pair with it? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
